top: fall in sales of NPK complex fertilisers, April–September 2026, the steepest of any major fertiliser.
rise in the price of a bag of NPK 12-32-16 or 10-26-26, to Rs 2,450, while DAP's price was held at Rs 1,350.

sections.h2: Sales fell most where the price moved

chart.title: NPK complexes fell furthest; DAP, whose price was held, barely moved
chart.sub: Change in sales, April–September 2026 vs a year earlier, %.
chart.source: Industry data via Rural Voice and The Wire (26 Oct 2026).

sections.means: Sales fell most for the fertilisers whose retail price rose, and least for DAP, whose price was capped.
sections.todo: Watch the rabi subsidy rates when they are announced, since they decide whether DAP stays at Rs 1,350.

sections.h2: NPK bags became dearer per kilogram of nutrient, while DAP and urea did not

chart.title: A farmer pays about Rs 82 per kg of nutrient for 12-32-16, against Rs 42 for DAP
chart.sub: Rs per kg of nutrient (N+P+K), kharif 2026. Kharif 2025 in the note.
chart.source: Rural Voice (Madhya Pradesh federation and company quotes); this blog's arithmetic.

sections.means: A farmer who switches from a complex fertiliser to DAP and urea pays less but gets no potash.
sections.todo: Check whether the government's push for balanced nutrition is backed by prices that make complexes affordable.

sections.h2: NPK sales ran ahead of new supply, while urea and MOP had supply to spare

chart.title: NPK sales ran 0.8 million tonnes ahead of new supply, drawing on stocks
chart.sub: Production plus imports minus sales, April–September 2026, million tonnes. Ignores opening stocks.
chart.source: Industry data via Rural Voice and The Wire; this blog's arithmetic.

sections.means: Urea was available and farmers bought less of it, which points to the weak monsoon; NPK was limited by price and supply.
sections.todo: Track NPK stocks into rabi, since the post says they are being run down while DAP stocks have built up.
